ideas.what: From K3 (exp59) onward, and in F1-final: --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=37800 (10.5 h) instead of 34200 (9.5 h). Keep DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=28800 (8.0 h) unchanged. Builder change in tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1849: add 37800 to the submission whitelist, extend tests/test_safetail.py (37800 allowed without --lab, other values still refused). Pre-register a runtime ledger in CONTEXT §e. Each rider reports its per-clip delta from its own dummy: 'repair Xs' and 'detection+edges Xs' vs K2. Forecast = 7.73 h (L35 upper bound) + 106 clips x sum of deltas, x1.15 for jitter. A rider that pushes the forecast past 8.0 h must shift DIVINS_DEADLINE_S by the same delta (REPAIR stays capped at 10.5 h), or it is dropped. R5 admission ceiling for these builds becomes 10.5 h.
ideas.why_now: Two new facts. (a) The limit is 12 h, not 9 h. (b) The hidden rerun covers public and private in ONE run, and L34/L35 bound it: K2 <= 7.73 h + 106 x 4.4 s (lowrefine) = 7.86 h. A 9.5 h deadline therefore leaves 2.5 h of the 12 h unused, in exactly the worlds where it matters: a slower rerun. Our 6 dummies show GPU 208-268 s per clip per shard (+-12%) and setup 257-636 s. At N=106 and 1.25x slower, the run needs ~10.65 h. The 9.5 h deadline then degrades ~26 clips; 10.5 h degrades ~3. Timeout safety: FD measured the degraded path at 28.2 s/clip (28.1/32.2/6.6/45.7 s). The worst post-deadline tail is 106 x 28 x 1.5 = 1.24 h, which ends at <= 11.74 h. In the 'N~199 on faster hardware' world, s~0.55, so the tail is ~0.85 h. Keep the 8.0 h insertion gate. It protects repair time: with safetail, one degraded clip costs ~0.015-0.02/N, while one clip's insertion is worth ~0.001/N (#35-#34), so 1 degraded clip ~= 15-55 insertions. This is a new mechanism relative to the refuted 'budget-aware deadline' (v3 schedule json: all-or-nothing rule). It is a fixed later threshold backed by measured degraded-path cost, with no new code path.

ideas.expected_gain: 0 in the normal world, where K2 ends <= ~7.9 h and nothing fires. In a >=1.2x-slower rerun it is worth +0.003..+0.01 on both boards, with P ~0.03-0.05 (guess). E ~= +0.0001..+0.0004 private. It also turns latencies of 9.5-10.5 h from 'unproven' into 'admissible' under R5.
ideas.runtime_cost: 0 s: only the point where degradation starts moves. Worst case ends at 10.5 h + 1.24 h = 11.74 h < 12 h.
ideas.test_gate: Builder unit tests pass (69 + new cases). The K3 dummy log shows 'SAFETAIL: repair deadline 37800s, divins deadline 28800s'. The K3 dummy CSV sha256 equals the same K3 built with 34200, since neither fires on the dummy. No LB slot and no lab arm: it rides inside K3. Certify by latency: L(K3) <= 10.5 h proves nothing fired, and L <= 8.0 h proves the insertion gate did not fire either.
ideas.risk: Timeout needs > 190 clips left at the deadline at dummy speed, which the step-0 bounds rule out. The main risk is a builder or test slip; the whitelist test covers it. Do not also move DIVINS later: that trades repair time for insertions at a 15-55:1 loss.

ideas.what: Optional K4 rider, only if agent hours remain after K3/K3b and only together with E7 tempfuse (same count-guard code, same LOEO test). In the x138 predict-patch cell, after the base 8-view D4 encodes, run ONE extra identity-view encode per model (primary and secondary) on the diagonal half-cell phase input zarr[t, :, 2::4, 2::4]. _load_frame is strided, so it sees only phase (0,0) today and 15/16 of the xy pixels are never read. Shift the phase logits back by half a cell: bilinear, i.e. a 2x2 mean onto the base grid. Blend the phase into the existing det_logits as a 9th view of each model before the 0.2/0.8 primary/secondary blend. Leave unet_out untouched, so the V1284 head and edge features stay byte-identical. Apply tempfuse's per-frame quantile count guard (nodes +-1%). Knob BIOHUB_PHASETTA_ENABLE: 0 = byte-identical.
ideas.why_now: Headroom now pays for it: +2 encodes/window ~= +26 s per clip per shard, i.e. +13 s/clip wall on 2 shards, i.e. +0.38 h at N=106. That puts the forecast at 8.24 h, so H1 must also be in and DIVINS_DEADLINE_S must move +0.4 h in lock-step. Phase is the only in-distribution TTA axis x138 has not used. D4 is saturated (8+8 detection views, 8+8 edge-feature views, 8 DeepCenter views). z-flip and axis-flip are closed (R9). Temporal is E7. The D4 views re-use the SAME pixels, so they average model variance only. A new phase adds independent shot noise, the one thing a view can add. It targets faint nuclei that never cross 0.965 anywhere, a different subset from readmit (>=0.965 ILP discards) and gapfill (0.5-0.965 peaks inside gaps). This differs from the refuted v2 polyphase idea, which aimed at localisation (<= +0.0005 on top of the head). Here the aim is detection recall.

A half-cell bilinear shift blurs the phase map, so peak calibration moves; the count guard is mandatory. Node-count multiplier. Deadline coupling: if the gates are not moved in lock-step, the 8.0 h insertion gate fires on the tail. It competes with K3/K3b for agent hours (R10: it goes after E7).

plan_critique: Under the runtime lens: (1) The ~4 h is insurance, not a budget. No reviewed idea was killed by runtime alone: a grep of all research/wf_ideas_v3/v_*_value.json finds only simview (+0.0002 regardless) and optional-nodes (value ~0). The GPU-hungry class of extra detector/edge views is 0/5 on our LB (probes 5, 12, 16, 19; secondary swaps -0.007..-0.025). x138 already runs 8+8 detection views, 8+8 edge-feature views and 8 DeepCenter views. There is no anytime component where more compute gives better answers: the ILP finishes in 5-90 s against a 1200 s timeout, and Hungarian relink and safe-div are exact. So do not open 'more TTA/seeds/kNN/ILP candidates/2nd V1284 pass/readmit radii' lines. The only unexplored in-distribution TTA axes are temporal (E7, already planned) and xy phase (H2, optional). (2) Timing numbers to carry into §e. K2 forecast <= 7.86 h: L35 upper bound + 106 x 4.4 s lowrefine, from K2 dummy repair 127.3 vs exp57b 122.9 s/clip. The insertion gate at 8.0 h is only +0.14 h above that, which is fine. It is the gate that protects repair time: 1 degraded clip ~= 15-55 clips of insertion. Do NOT move it later on its own. The repair deadline of 9.5 h wastes the 12 h limit in slow-rerun worlds. Degraded path = 28.2 s/clip (FD dummy), so 10.5 h is timeout-safe (H1). (3) Forecasts should carry +-15% jitter: the 6 dummies show GPU 208-268 s per clip per shard and setup 257-636 s. R5 'proof by latency' stays the right instrument. Make sure the poller runs 26 Sep 00:00-09:00 UTC, so L(K2) is measured: 5 polls came back empty on 25 Sep. (4) Add a runtime ledger line to tools/dummy_gates.py: per-clip delta of 'repair' and 'detection+edges' vs the K2 dummy, plus the forecast at N=106. That way every rider (forkmid ~0, DeepCenter threshold ~0, tempfuse ~0 GPU) is budget-checked mechanically before S12 consolidation. (5) R6/N1 and 'no speed-ups' stay correct: H1 buys most of N1's slow-world insurance with zero code. Pipelined repair on the GPUs, idle for ~3.5 h during the CPU repair phase, is only worth building if H2 or another runtime rider pushes the forecast past ~9 h. (6) F2 = exp52 has no timer. That remains the right hedge for a 'rerun much slower' world.
